title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701)
note: Book the exam date first; Professor Messer's free videos plus one practice-exam bundle is the standard student path.

title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
note: Hands-on labs matter more than videos; the free tier covers everything the exam asks.

title: Certified Kubernetes Administrator
note: Performance-based exam: practice in a real cluster, not flashcards.

title: Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer
note: Google's own Skills Boost path is enough; budget extra time on IAM.

title: HashiCorp Terraform Associate
note: The cheapest cloud credential with real signal; pairs well with AWS SAA.

title: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate
note: Free Edition is enough to practice every topic on the exam guide.

title: Databricks Certified Data Analyst Associate
note: SQL-heavy; if you can write the queries in this app's warehouse you are most of the way there.

title: Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)
note: PMP itself requires 36 months of experience; CAPM is the student-eligible version employers accept in its place.

title: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt
note: The Coursera specialization is what most students list; ASQ's exam is the gold standard if you have $400 more.

title: Tableau Desktop Specialist
note: Free student license; build two dashboards from public data and the exam is straightforward.

title: CFA Program Level I
note: A semester of study; the student-scholarship cuts the fee to ~$350. Say 'Level I candidate' once registered.

title: Bloomberg Market Concepts (BMC)
note: Free through Pamplin's Bloomberg terminals; the quickest credential on this list.

title: Financial Modeling & Valuation Analyst (FMVA)
note: Recognized in banking recruiting; the Excel modeling modules are the part that shows up in interviews.

title: Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) Exam
note: Open to students with no sponsor; a real differentiator for sales & trading applicants.

title: CPA exam — first section (FAR or AUD)
note: Firms want to see you registered and one section scheduled before the internship; Becker and UWorld are the usual prep.

title: CPA licensure (all four sections + 150 credit hours)
note: A post-graduation goal for most; what an internship posting really means is 'CPA-track' — see the in-progress entry.

title: Certified Management Accountant
note: Student membership cuts the fee roughly in half; Part 1 alone is a credible resume line.

title: Certified Fraud Examiner
note: Requires experience to hold the credential, but student associate membership and the prep course are what forensic teams look for.

title: Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel Expert
note: Small, fast, and it answers the 'how good is your Excel really' question before it is asked.

title: Alteryx Designer Core Certification
note: Free exam, free student license; Big Four audit teams use Alteryx daily.

title: Python for Everybody Specialization
note: Audit it free; the thing to put on the resume is one small project that uses it, not the certificate.

title: SQL for Data Science
note: Then write real queries: this app's warehouse is a fine place to practice.

title: Java Programming and Software Engineering Fundamentals
note: Skip if you already have CS 2114 on your transcript — list the course instead.

title: Git and GitHub Foundations
note: A weekend. Then make your projects public — a green contribution graph is the credential.

title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials
note: The free on-ramp; if you like it, the Solutions Architect Associate is the credential.

title: Docker for the Absolute Beginner
note: Containerize one of your own projects and add the Dockerfile to the repo.

title: Apache Spark Programming with Databricks
note: Free self-paced; leads straight into the Data Engineer Associate exam.

title: Machine Learning Specialization
note: The standard. Pair with one Kaggle notebook you can talk through in an interview.

title: MIT 6.824 Distributed Systems (lectures + labs)
note: Hard and worth it; finishing the Raft lab is a real interview story.

title: Excel Skills for Business Specialization
note: Then rebuild one real model from scratch without a template; that is what the interview tests.

title: Financial Modeling Fundamentals
note: The one banks recognize; Pamplin's finance club often has a group discount.

title: Valuation and DCF Modeling
note: Build the model for one public company you actually follow and bring it to the interview.

title: Consulting Presentations: Slide Structure and Storylines
note: Free through VT's LinkedIn Learning access; the skill is storyline, not formatting.

title: Case Interview Prep with a Partner (Casebook + 20 live cases)
provider: The Consulting Group at Virginia Tech / Management Consulted
note: Twenty live cases with a partner beats any book; the campus consulting clubs run them every week.

title: Market Sizing Drills
note: Ten drills out loud; the interviewer grades the structure, not the number.

title: Stakeholder Management for Consultants
note: Mostly a vocabulary; a student org leadership role is the real evidence.

title: Introduction to Financial Accounting
note: If ACIS 2115 is on your transcript, list that instead.

title: US GAAP Fundamentals
note: Firms provide this on day one; the resume line is the intermediate accounting course you already took.

title: Financial Statement Analysis
note: Free; then pull one 10-K and write a one-page read of it.

title: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
note: Long. For an accounting or consulting posting, the Databricks Data Analyst Associate is faster and more specific.

title: Alteryx Designer Core learning path
note: Free student license; finish the path and take the free Core exam the same week.

title: Tableau eLearning: Desktop I
note: Free for students; publish one dashboard to Tableau Public and link it.

title: Statistics with Python Specialization
note: If STAT 3005/3006 is on your transcript, list the course; otherwise this.

title: Bloomberg Terminal training (BMC + terminal hours)
note: Pamplin has terminals; log real hours and you can say so in the interview.

title: Introduction to Linux (LFS101)
note: Free; use it daily on a VM for a month and it sticks.
